text:
Long ago, in a faraway land, there lived a poor old man. He had no wealth and no land. He owned only one treasure: a horse. But this was no ordinary horse. It was the finest, most beautiful, and fastest horse in the whole region. The old man loved it like his own child. He fed it himself, gave it water himself, and combed its mane every single day.

The horse’s fame reached the king. He summoned the old man to the palace and said, “I’ve heard you own a remarkable horse. Sell it to me, and I’ll give you so much treasure that you’ll never have to work again for the rest of your life.”

Servants carried in huge chests full of gold and silver. Everyone gasped. But the old man thought for a moment, then shook his head. “Forgive me, Your Majesty, but to me this horse is not property. He is a friend. And a friend cannot be sold.”

The news quickly spread across the village. People gathered outside the old man’s house and began to laugh at him.

“You fool!” they said. “You barely get by, and some days you can’t even afford bread. If you’d agreed, you’d be rich, and your children and grandchildren would live in comfort!”

The old man said nothing. He only smiled.

The next morning, he went to the stable and found it empty. The horse was gone! The door was open, and the horse had vanished without a trace. The old man searched everywhere but couldn’t find him.

The neighbors gathered again. Now they pretended to sympathize, but they said exactly what they had been dying to say: “See? If you’d sold him to the king yesterday, you’d be rich right now. Now you have no horse and no money. You’ll starve with nothing to eat!”

Then the old man answered quietly: “Yes, my horse is gone. And I have no fortune. But whether this is good or bad, no one knows yet. The rest is only your opinion.”

The villagers shrugged and walked away, chuckling. “The old man has lost his mind,” they thought.

Fifteen days passed. One morning at dawn, a noise came from the hills. The old man stepped outside and couldn’t believe his eyes: his horse was coming home, and behind him ran twelve wild horses! It turned out nobody had stolen him. He had simply longed for freedom, wandered into the mountains, joined a herd of wild horses, and led them back with him.

The whole village gathered in the old man’s yard again, this time with their mouths hanging open. “You truly are a wise man!” they said. “We laughed at you for nothing. Now your horse is back, and you have twelve more. You’re rich! You’ve escaped poverty!”

The old man replied in the same calm voice: “You’re rushing to conclusions again. Yes, my horse returned, and he brought twelve horses. But whether that is good or bad, we don’t know yet. The rest is only your opinion.”

The villagers looked at one another. What kind of man was this? Even after such good fortune, he wasn’t happy?

The old man had one son. The young man worked, earned money, and the two of them lived on it and bought bread. When he saw the wild horses, he decided to tame them. Every day he tried to ride one of them.

One day, a strong and stubborn horse threw him off. He fell hard and broke his leg.

The villagers gathered once more. This time they hardly hid their mockery: “Now real hunger begins! Your only son can’t work. Who will bring you bread now? These wild horses have been your misfortune!”

The old man said softly: “My son’s leg is broken, that’s true. But whether this is good or bad, we don’t know yet. The rest is only your opinion.”

The people laughed again, but this time silently, so the old man wouldn’t hear.

A long time passed. One day, terrible news came from the border: a huge army from a neighboring country was marching on their land. War began. The country was in grave danger, and its soldiers were losing.

In desperation, the king ordered that every man able to fight be gathered and sent against the enemy. It was clear that many would not return from this war. They would either die or be captured and spend the rest of their lives in slavery.

Soldiers went from village to village, taking away young men. They came to the old man’s house too. But his son’s leg was broken. “This one is no use in war,” they decided, and left him behind.

The villagers came to the old man in tears. Every mother and father had sent a child to war and might never see them again.

“You truly are wise,” they wept. “They took all our children. Yet your son is still with you, even with a broken leg!”

The old man looked at them with warmth and said, “I wanted to tell you something. You’ve caught the habit of judging too quickly. When my horse disappeared, when he came back, when my son broke his leg, I knew only one thing: whether an event in life is good or bad, only time can show. And we see only one moment of it.”

Moral: Never judge life by a single moment. Today’s misfortune may become tomorrow’s rescue, and today’s joy may be tomorrow’s test. Watch events with patience and don’t rush to conclusions. Time reveals the true meaning of everything.

tr.title: Bilmaymiz
paragraphs: Qadim zamonda, olis bir o’lkada bir chol yashar ekan. Uning mol-mulki ham, boyligi ham yo’q ekan. Faqat bitta oti bor ekan. Ammo bu ot oddiy ot emas, butun o’lkadagi eng zo’r, eng chiroyli, eng chopqir ot ekan. Chol uni o’z farzandidek yaxshi ko’rar, har kuni o’zi yedirib, o’zi suv berib, yolini tarab qo’yar ekan.

Otning shuhrati podshohning qulog’iga ham yetibdi. Podshoh cholni saroyiga chaqirtiribdi va debdi: «Eshitishimcha, sening shunday otingi bor ekan. Uni menga sot, men senga shunchalik xazina beray, umringning oxirigacha ishlamasdan yashaysan.»

Podshoh oldiga katta-katta sandiqlarni keltiribdi. Ichi oltin va kumushga to’la ekan. Hamma hayratda qolibdi. Lekin chol bir oz o’ylab turib, boshini chayqabdi: «Kechirasiz, podshohim, bu ot men uchun mol emas, do’stim. Do’stni sotib bo’lmaydi.»
Bu gap tezda butun qishloqqa tarqabdi. Odamlar cholning uyiga yig’ilib, uning ustidan kula boshlabdi.
«Sen ahmoq ekansan!» deyishibdi. «O’zing kunda zo’rg’a kun ko’rasan, ba’zan non ham topa olmaysan. Rozi bo’lganingda, katta boylikka ega bo’lardingki, bolalaring ham, nevaralaring ham to’q yashardi!»
Chol indamabdi, faqat jilmayibdi.
Ertasiga ertalab chol otxonaga borsa, otxona bo’m-bo’sh. Ot yo’q! Eshik ochiq, ot izsiz g’oyib bo’libdi. Chol atrofni qidiribdi, ammo topa olmabdi.

Qo’shnilar yana yig’ilibdi. Endi ular afsus qilgan bo’lib, aslida tilga olmoqchi bo’lgan gapni aytishibdi: «Ana ko’rdingmi! Kecha podshohga sotganingda, hozir boyib yurgan bo’larding. Endi na oting bor, na boyliging. Hozir yana och qolib, non topa olmay o’lasan!»
Shunda chol sokin ovozda javob beribdi: «To’g’ri, otim yo’qoldi. Boyligim ham yo’q. Lekin bu yaxshilikmi yoki yomonlikmi, buni hali hech kim bilmaydi. Qolgani sizlarning taxminingiz, xolos.»
Odamlar yelka qisib, kulgancha tarqalishibdi. «Bu cholning aqli joyida emas», deb o’ylashibdi.

Orada o’n besh kun o’tibdi. Bir kuni tong otganda, tepalik tomondan qandaydir tovush eshitilibdi. Chol tashqariga chiqsa, ko’z oldida g’alati manzara: uning oti qaytib kelayotgan ekan, orqasidan esa o’n ikkita yovvoyi ot ergashib kelayotgan ekan! Ot o’g’irlanmagan ekan, shunchaki erkinlikni sog’inib, tog’larga ketib qolgan, u yerda yovvoyi otlar to’dasiga qo’shilib, ularni ergashtirib qaytgan ekan.

Qishloq xalqi yana cholning hovlisiga yig’ilibdi, endi esa hayratdan og’izlari ochilib qolibdi. «Sen chindan ham dono odam ekansan!» deyishibdi. «Biz sening ustingdan bekorga kulgan ekanmiz. Mana, otingni ham topding, yana o’n ikkita ot ortirding. Endi sen boy bo’lding, qashshoqlikdan qutuldin!»

Chol esa yana o’sha sokinlik bilan javob beribdi: «Siz yana shoshilib xulosa chiqaryapsiz. Ha, otim qaytdi, o’n ikkita ot bilan keldi. Lekin bu yaxshilikmi yoki yomonlikmi, hali bilmaymiz. Qolgani sizning taxminingiz.»
Odamlar bir-birining yuziga qarab, «Bu chol qanaqa odam o’zi?» deb o’ylashibdi. Axir bunday baxtdan keyin ham quvonmayaptimi?

Cholning yagona o’g’li bor ekan. U ishlab, otasi ikkalasiga non topib yeydigan yigit ekan. Yovvoyi otlarni ko’rib, ularni o’rgatmoqchi bo’libdi. Har kuni bir otni minishga urinib, qo’lga o’rgatayotgan ekan.
Bir kuni bitta kuchli, o’jar ot yigitni yelkasidan irg’itib yuboribdi. Yigit qattiq yiqilib, oyog’i sinibdi.

Qishloq xalqi yana yig’ilibdi. Bu safar ular deyarli ochiq kulishibdi: «Mana endi chin ochlik boshlandi! Cholning yagona farzandi ishlay olmaydi. Endi kim ularga non topib beradi? Bu yovvoyi otlar sening baxtsizliging bo’ldi!»
Chol faqat ohista dedi: «O’g’limning oyog’i sindi, bu rost. Lekin bu yaxshilikmi yoki yomonlikmi, hali bilmaymiz. Qolgani sizlarning taxminingiz, xolos.»
Odamlar yana uning ustidan kulishdi, lekin bu safar ichlarida, chol eshitmasin deb.

Oradan ancha vaqt o’tibdi. Bir kuni chegaradan qo’rqinchli xabar kelibdi: qo’shni mamlakatdan ulkan qo’shin bosib kelayotgan ekan. Urush boshlanibdi. Mamlakat qiyin ahvolga tushibdi, askarlar yutqaza boshlabdi.

Podshoh so’nggi chora sifatida mamlakatdagi urushga yaraydigan barcha yigitlarni to’plashga buyruq beribdi. Ularni dushman qarshisiga qo’yishibdi. Bu urushdan ularning ko’pi qaytmasligi aniq ekan. Yoki o’lib ketishardi, yoki asir tushib, umrbod qullikda yashashardi.
Askarlar qishloqma-qishloq yurib, yigitlarni olib ketishibdi. Cholning uyiga ham kelishibdi. Lekin o’g’lining oyog’i singan ekan. «Bu urushga yaramaydi», deb, uni qoldirib ketishibdi.
Qishloq xalqi yig’lab, cholning huzuriga kelibdi. Hamma onalar va otalar farzandini urushga jo’natgan, endi ularni qaytib ko’ra olmasliklari mumkin edi.
«Sen chindan ham dono ekansan», deb yig’lashibdi ular. «Bizning hamma farzandlarimizni olib ketishdi. Sen esa o’g’ling bilan birgasan, hatto oyog’i singan bo’lsa ham!»

Chol ularga mehr bilan qarabdi va debdi: «Men sizlarga aytmoqchi edim. Sizlar erta xulosa chiqarish kasaliga yo’liqqansizlar. Otim yo’qolganda ham, qaytganda ham, o’g’lim yiqilganda ham, men bir narsani bilardim. Hayotda biror voqea yaxshimi yoki yomonmi, buni faqat vaqt ko’rsatadi. Biz esa hayotning faqat bir lahzasini ko’ramiz, xolos.»

Qissadan hissa: Hayotning faqat bir lahzasiga qarab hukm chiqarma. Bugungi musibat ertaga najot bo’lishi mumkin, bugungi quvonch esa ertangi sinov bo’lishi mumkin. Voqealarni shoshilmay, sabr bilan kuzat. Vaqt hamma narsaning haqiqiy ma’nosini ochib beradi.

quiz.q: The old man sold his horse to the king.
The horse came back with twelve wild horses.
Why didn't the soldiers take the old man's son to war?
What does the old man always say about events?
o: Nobody knows yet if it is good or bad

quiz.q: Whether an event is good or bad, only ___ can show.
